localContext: Prospect Lefferts Gardens' tree-lined streets, community gardens, and mix of historic brownstones and apartment buildings create ideal nesting sites for wasps, hornets, yellow jackets, and carpenter bees. The neighborhood's proximity to Prospect Park and abundance of flowering gardens means stinging-insect activity is common from spring through fall — paper nests appear in soffit vents and wall cavities, carpenter bees drill into porch columns and trim, and yellow jackets build ground nests in garden beds. Professional nest treatment and removal is essential for homeowners along streets like Maple, Midwood, and Rutland Road.
